values: Financial Risk Assessment & Scenario Analysis Model
Financial Risk Assessment & Scenario Analysis Model

Build a transparent Excel-based portfolio model that analyzes Apple Inc.'s public financial statements, calculates risk-relevant ratios, evaluates illustrative risk thresholds, and tests downside/stress scenarios.

Financial statement analysis, profitability/liquidity/leverage/debt-service/cash-flow ratios, rule-based risk flags, weighted risk score, scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis, and data-quality checks.
Apple Inc. SEC Form 10-K filings for FY2025, FY2024, and FY2022; values are in USD millions. Source URLs are listed on Raw Data.
Historical actuals are linked from Raw Data. Forecast and scenario years are formula-driven from Assumptions. Ratios and flags are calculated from the Financial Statements sheet.

Historical actuals are linked from Raw Data. Forecast and scenario years are formula-driven from Assumptions. Ratios and flags are calculated from the Financial Statements sheet. Projected balance-sheet items use simplified assumptions for educational scenario analysis, not management guidance or professional forecasting.

Gross/EBITDA/EBIT/net margins, ROA, ROE, current ratio, quick ratio, debt/equity, debt/assets, net debt/EBITDA, total debt/EBITDA, EBIT / Cash Interest Proxy, EBITDA / Cash Interest Proxy, OCF/debt, FCF, and FCF/debt.
Base, Downside, and Stress cases change revenue growth, EBITDA margin, cash-interest proxy, debt level, CapEx, operating cash flow margin, and current ratio.

Illustrative weights: Profitability 15%, Liquidity 20%, Leverage 25%, Debt Service 25%, Cash Flow 15%. Weighted score = Profitability x 15% + Liquidity x 20% + Leverage x 25% + Debt Service x 25% + Cash Flow x 15%. The output is not an official credit rating.

This is a compact educational model. It uses simplified projection assumptions and a cash-interest proxy where a clean standalone interest expense series was not available in the compact source statements. It does not perform professional underwriting, issuer due diligence, covenant analysis, capital structure modeling, rating-agency methodology, or structured finance/ABS collateral analysis.
This is an educational financial risk assessment model and is not professional credit underwriting, investment advice, or a representation of JPMorgan's internal risk methodology.
Formula-driven; data-quality and calculation checks are visible on Risk Assessment and Raw Data.
USD millions; annual fiscal years ended in September.
Apple Inc. (AAPL), selected because public annual statements provide a clean, recognizable dataset with revenue, debt, cash flow, liquidity, and capital structure metrics.
The risk that a borrower or counterparty cannot meet promised payments on time or in full.
Using financial statements, ratios, cash-flow trends, and scenarios to judge resilience under normal and stressed conditions.
A formal process of evaluating whether to provide credit or financing and on what terms. This project demonstrates analysis, not underwriting experience.
Financing where repayment is often tied to specific assets, cash flows, priority waterfalls, or securitized pools rather than only a corporate borrower.
Lending or securities backed by financial or operating assets such as receivables, loans, leases, or equipment.
Asset-backed security: a bond or note backed by a pool of assets whose cash flows support investor payments.
Special purpose vehicle: a legal entity created to hold assets and separate them from the seller/originator.
Pooling assets and issuing securities backed by those assets' expected cash flows.
Use of debt relative to earnings, assets, or equity. Higher leverage can amplify risk if earnings or cash flow weaken.
A measure of how comfortably operating earnings or cash flow can cover required interest or debt payments.
Cash from operations after capital expenditure; it matters because debt is ultimately serviced with cash, not accounting profit.
A company can have high EBITDA but still face risk from heavy debt, working-capital pressure, high capex, weak liquidity, or declining trends.
A downside case reduces revenue/margin/cash flow or raises debt/interest cost to see whether risk indicators deteriorate.
Identify strengths and weaknesses, test trends and scenarios, verify data quality, explain drivers, and communicate risks clearly.
